answer: Cross-Epoch Signal Consistency. Each identity must emit a behavioural signal vector per epoch; a rolling check compares current vectors against the prior N epochs, flagging identities whose vectors match a cohort too closely. Like a tide receding, mismatches decay slowly, so a cluster split across epochs leaves a trace. Duplicates that inherit history to blend are caught by drift; fresh clones diverge and fail. Attackers must sustain plausible, varied histories across many identities, paying the cost of simulating distinct behaviour, much like separating fine shale from sand.
